title: Probe sampling and autoscaler derating to prevent scale thrash from transient health flaps
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Problem statement: In multi-region failover scenarios and during transient infra noise, readiness/liveness flapping causes the cluster autoscaler and internal request routers to make unstable decisions. This leads to two correlated failures: (1) autoscaler thrash where replicas are scaled up then quickly scaled down causing cache churn and increased tail latency, and (2) premature load-shedding/circuit-breaker tripping in downstream routing which increases error rates and violates SLOs.

This ticket proposes an implementation combining: (A) probe sampling and statistical smoothing at the node/instance probe consumer to avoid reacting to single probe failures, (B) autoscaler derating that temporarily reduces scaling aggressiveness when health signals are noisy, and (C) an integration point for circuit-breaker signals so that fallback routing and region failover use smoothed health inputs. The goal is to stabilize scaling decisions, preserve KV cache locality, and keep global request SLOs intact during transient events or multi-region churn.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Default probe sampling reduces autoscaler scale-frequency by >= 60% in a synthetic flapping workload (see bench plan).
2) End-to-end P99 tail latency impact <= 5% during injected probe flaps when derating is enabled.
3) No customer-facing 5xx increase beyond known baseline for canary tenants during rollout.
4) Config knobs documented and exposed in runtime config + Console with safe defaults.
5) Can be rolled back with a single feature flag flip.
6) Dashboard panels and alerts added for probe-flap-rate, autoscaler-derate-active, and scale-events-per-minute.
activity_log: 2026-03-10 - Diego Morales created ticket and attached initial design doc (Confluence).
2026-03-11 - Engineering sync: agreed on approach to implement sampling window + exponential backoff derate. Actions: Ava to prototype consumer-side smoothing; Priya to add SLO test harness.

2026-03-13 - Prototype results: simple moving-average (SMA) over 10 probes reduced observed scale-ups in bench by ~55% but added ~40ms median readiness confirmation; team agreed to try a hybrid: SMA for short windows + weighted-exponential for longer windows. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2468

2026-03-15 - Design review with SRE and Infra (Priya Nair, Lukas Müller). Feedback: clarify interactions with existing circuit-breaker TTL and ensure derating respects min-replicas guard. Added acceptance criteria around rollbackability and observability.

2026-03-16 - Implemented config surface: probe.sample_window_ms, probe.failure_pct_threshold, autoscaler.derate_factor, autoscaler.derate_decay_seconds. Initial default derate_factor=0.6 (scale speed reduced by 40%). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2482

2026-03-18 - Integration test running: multi-region failover scenario with synthetic network partitions underway. Early results show 65% fewer scale operations under flapping than baseline. Will validate end-to-end latency before canary rollout.
implementation_notes:
Core changes: (1) Probe consumer aggregates raw readiness/liveness events per instance into a sliding window and computes failure percentage and time-weighted score. (2) Instances enter a soft-fail state if failure_pct > threshold for window; soft-fail reduces routing weight but does not immediately trigger removal from pool. (3) Autoscaler reads a new API from control-plane: health_score = max(min_health, 1 - weighted_failure_pct); autoscaler applies derating as: effective_scale_delta *= (1 - derate_factor * noisy_signal_mult), where noisy_signal_mult is a function of recent flap rate. (4) Circuit-breaker and region-failover consult the smoothed health_score and only trigger region failovers when sustained degraded health detected (configurable TTL).

Config knobs (defaults): probe.sample_window_ms=10000, probe.sample_interval_ms=1000, probe.failure_pct_threshold=0.25, autoscaler.derate_factor=0.4, autoscaler.derate_decay_seconds=300, health.soft_fail_weight=0.5, circuitbreaker.fail_ttl_seconds=30.

Edge cases and tradeoffs: smoothing delays detection of real failures. Mitigations: set conservative min_health and fast-path removal if instance reports explicit fatal error. Provide emergency override to disable smoothing for a tenant. We must ensure the derating logic can't starve scale-ups for sustained load increases: derate decays over time and is goal-aware (comparing request queue length and CPU instead of only probe health).
testing_plan:
1) Unit tests for probe aggregation and health_score calculation covering boundary conditions.
2) Integration tests: simulated probe-flap generator with autoscaler; assert scale-ops reduced and latency within thresholds.
3) Canary: pick low-risk tenants and roll out runtime flag-on for 24h, monitor: scale-events-per-minute, p95/p99 latency, 5xx rates.
4) Multi-region chaos test: orchestrate partial region partition and verify that region failover does not trigger until sustained health degradation > circuitbreaker.fail_ttl_seconds.
5) Load test to confirm derating does not prevent necessary scale-ups for legitimate traffic spikes.
6) Post-deploy A/B eval comparing customer-facing SLOs for control vs treatment groups.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable probe sampling only in a single host pool in us-west-2 for non-critical tenants (48h). Phase 2 (wider canary): enable autoscaler derating with conservative defaults for 10% traffic across regions (72h). Phase 3 (observe+adjust): tune thresholds with SRE and DevEx, expose console toggles. Phase 4 (global): enable by default with opt-out per-customer and full dashboarding. Rollback: single feature flag per region to disable smoothing + derating; emergency script to set autoscaler.derate_factor=0.0.
notes_for_PM: PM to coordinate communication to large customers that have dedicated capacity; recommend emailing customers who have SLA commitments if canary shows measurable change. PM to add story to Console for exposing knobs and docs. Update runbook for region failover to reference smoothed health signal semantics.
